private_notes: Reader: Haiku scanned all 359 blocks and the ten main filings and proposed 93 candidates (scan.json, 34 marked uncertain); the editor (Opus) read the full argument independently, sourced, selected and wrote the cards, and only then read the Codex set.

From the Codex set (read after this set was complete): the circuit-split map (Maxwell’s cert reply p. 3; the government did not dispute the split), the § 3621(b) / § 3632(d)(4)(C) side-by-side (marks rebalanced: one operative phrase per provision rather than two phrases favoring the petitioner), and § 3624(g)(3) at Barber’s mootness answer.

Not adopted from Codex: Preiser at 0:26 (overlaps the question presented; Preiser is carded at Barber’s “Under Preiser” instead); a Skinner holding card (Kagan’s point concerns its language, so an excerpt is shown); a DIG definition sourced to a dissent (the government’s own brief is used); a § 3624(a) / prerelease comparison at 58:45 (Jackson reads § 3624(a) aloud).

Read aloud, so not carded: Hansford’s § 2241 and § 3621(b) quotations (wording differs slightly from the statute; the § 3621(b) card shows the exact text), Barber’s Morrissey definition of parole, Jackson’s reading of § 3624(a).
Hansford’s “3634(d)(4)(C)” is § 3632(d)(4)(C); the card cites the correct section. Her “complete release” paraphrase is not the Fifth Circuit’s test, so the decision-below card quotes the opinion.
January 22, 2027 is labelled as BOP’s projected date of eligibility for transfer to a halfway house (U.S. brief), not a release date as Barber says.

Neutrality: the JA 17 record card is the page Hansford cites, shown without comment on whether exhaustion was satisfied; the escape-statute and Koray cards show what Barnes relies on, not whether it is decisive; the case timeline gives dates only.

Omitted: Wolff, Morrissey, Jones v. Hendrix, Camreta, Rivera-Perez, Osorio-Calderon, Gonzalez v. Herrera (passing references or unverified facts); “capable of repetition”, “voluntary cessation”, “collateral consequences” glossaries (general doctrine not in the filings); Puerto Rico transfer examples (not in the sources).
Renderer: the subscribe overlay covers the card area during the first two blocks of each later section, so St. Cyr starts at block 351; the workbench now checks this.
Sinochem is hidden by default as a passing reference.
